note: Explicit, visible accepted-risk records for the RoamLink production readiness gate (RL-081). Recorded by Worker C at gate-construction time; ratification by the Tech Lead is required at merge. These records NEVER weaken a gate criterion: every criterion is still evaluated literally — an unmet row covered here is reported as a `gap` row carrying its risk ids, and any uncovered failure still fails the gate. The MVP gate (RL-080) has NO acceptance mechanism by dispatch: its failing criteria are findings for the Tech Lead, and the headline MVP finding (the §11 SLO criterion, see AR-002) is what currently fails RL-080.

risks.title: Dogfood scenarios did not wire the observability structured logger (REMEDIATED — the world now composes the correlated logger)
risks.justification: At gate-construction time the dogfood scenarios did not wire the observability structured logger: correlation IDs were proven end-to-end through audit events only, and structured-log records were not part of the dogfood evidence. REMEDIATED on work/rl-slo-wiring-remediation (MVP-3 remediation worker, Wave 6): the dogfood world now composes createCorrelatedLogger over createInMemoryLogSink with the manual correlation carrier, and scenario 1 emits an §11 SLO evaluation through logSloEvaluation under the journey's correlation-id family, asserting the log record carries the correlation id and the SLO's own redaction-safe fields. The production gate's OBS:logs-correlation row now passes on real structured-log evidence.
risks.exposure: None remaining: structured-log records with correlation IDs are now part of the dogfood evidence (tests/dogfood/src/world.ts + scenario 1's logSloEvaluation assertion).
risks.remediation: LANDED: tests/dogfood/src/world.ts (correlated logger + in-memory sink + manual carrier on the §11 SLO plane) and scenario-1's structured-log assertion (correlation id + slo/slo_state fields). Re-run pnpm production-gate on the remediation commit: PRD-3 passes with zero gap rows.
risks.reviewBy: ratified at merge (remediation landed; PRD-3 gap-free)

risks.title: No §11 SLO was instrumented or referenced in the dogfood/load suites (REMEDIATED — the MVP-gate blocker is closed)
risks.justification: spec/architecture.md §11 lists nine SLOs the product must measure. The observability primitives (RL-052: makeServiceLevelObjective, SloEventRecorder, burn rates, health/metrics/log composition) can instrument every one of them — proven green by tests/release-gates/test/contract-deep.test.ts — but at gate-construction time NO dogfood or load assertion referenced any §11 SLO name and no product surface wired §11-named SLOs, which is why the MVP release gate (RL-080) failed its SLO criterion. REMEDIATED on work/rl-slo-wiring-remediation (MVP-3 remediation worker, Wave 6): packages/observability gained the §11 SLO instrumentation surface (PRODUCT_SLO_IDS, the nine roamlink_slo_<slug> metric constants, registerProductSloMetrics, createProductSloRecorder); the reconciliation engine emits its durable-action §11 measurements through an optional structural sloObserver; domain-experience exposes the pure intentSatisfactionOf mapping; and the dogfood/load suites record + assert all nine SLOs through the real recorder. Both gates now exit 0 (MVP-3: 9/9 rows pass). The record is retained for history: the gap was real, visible, and closed by the documented remediation rather than by weakening the gate.
risks.exposure: None remaining as a verification gap: the end-to-end suites now provide mechanical SLO evidence (dogfood scenarios assert all nine §11 SLOs; the load REC suite asserts SLO-E emission-volume invariants). At gate-construction time the exposure was a verification-coverage gap only — no runtime defect.
risks.remediation: LANDED: packages/observability/src/slo/slo-metrics.ts (the §11 surface), packages/reconciliation/src/slo-emission.ts + engine/boundary sloObserver wiring, packages/domain-experience/src/decision/intent-satisfaction.ts, tests/dogfood scenario/world/journey SLO wiring and assertions for all nine SLOs, tests/load SLO-E emission invariants, package tests for every new module (observability 76, reconciliation 82, domain-experience 116 green). Re-run pnpm mvp-gate and pnpm production-gate on the remediation commit: both exit 0 with MVP-3 9/9 rows passing.
risks.reviewBy: ratified at merge (remediation landed; gates green)

risks.title: spec/current-state.md still claims 'no production feature implementation started' / 'Repository state: greenfield'
risks.justification: The implemented tree contradicts spec/current-state.md's header claims: 25 packages + 3 apps + 7 verification suites with green tests exist on main. The dispatch for the release-gate worker explicitly forbids editing spec/* ('the gates MEASURE the spec, they don't change it'), so this documented inconsistency is recorded as an explicit gap for the Tech Lead instead of being silently patched.
risks.exposure: Documentation only: a reader of spec/current-state.md is misled about implementation status. No code, test or gate behavior depends on the stale claims (the gates verify the tree, not the doc's prose).
risks.remediation: The Tech Lead refreshes spec/current-state.md's status block to reflect the implemented tree (minutes of work); the production gate's DOCS:current-state row then turns green without any gate change.
risks.reviewBy: at merge of the release-gates branch

risks.title: RL-074-F1: secret-shaped provider references are accepted into commerce payment records
risks.justification: A malicious provider returning a JWT-shaped string as its payment 'provider reference' is accepted at admission and persisted into the commerce read model (charset permits dots/base64url). spec/data-model.md 'Privacy' says secrets/credentials are never persisted in ordinary domain tables. Exposure is bounded: the value is provider-supplied opaque REFERENCE data, not a RoamLink credential; PEM-shaped values are rejected by the charset; the repo's own RL-054 scanner flags the persisted record afterward (detection exists, admission-time enforcement does not). Fixing it means editing packages/domain-commerce — explicitly outside the release-gate worker's scope — so the finding is accepted for this release with the recorded remediation.
risks.exposure: A secret-shaped value could be persisted in a commerce record and surfaced in read models; it is not a usable credential and is detectable by the existing scanner sweep.
risks.remediation: Run assertNoSecretMaterial over provider-supplied reference fields at commerce admission, or further restrict the charset (e.g. no '.'). Minimal reproducer already pinned in tests/security S-6 so the fix flips an explicit assertion.

risks.title: RL-074-F2: the auth session record's tokenDigest field name is scanner-flagged
risks.justification: The RL-054 secret-shape scanner flags the FIELD NAME (key-name detector, 'token' fragment) of AuthSessionRecord.tokenDigest. The VALUE is a non-invertible SHA-256 digest — possession of the digest is not possession of the credential (verifySession requires the token; only its digest is compared) — so the substance of RL-LOCK-016 holds (proven: the live token appears in no persisted record; the digest is 64-hex). The finding records a naming-discipline inconsistency with the enterprise package's deliberate keyRef/signingKeyRef naming, which blocks wiring a repo-wide scanner sweep as a CI gate over ALL persisted records without an allow-list decision.
risks.exposure: Scanner noise / discipline inconsistency only; no secret material is exposed.
risks.remediation: Rename (e.g. tokenVerificationDigest) or make an explicit, documented scanner allowance for digest fields — orchestrator call. Minimal reproducer pinned in tests/security S-2.
risks.reviewBy: when the scanner sweep is wired as a CI gate

risks.title: RL-074-F3: double session revocation surfaces a typed CAS conflict instead of an idempotent no-op
risks.justification: Revoking an ALREADY-REVOKED session through a second, distinct command throws ConflictError (REVISION_CONFLICT) because the service re-saves the unchanged record whose revision no longer satisfies the stored+1 precondition. The behavior fails CLOSED (the session stays revoked; nothing reopens) — an ergonomics/idempotency gap, not a vulnerability. Fixing it means editing packages/auth — outside the release-gate worker's scope.
risks.exposure: Operator-visible typed error on a redundant revoke; no state corruption, no reopening of revoked sessions.
risks.remediation: Skip the save when the record is already revoked (return the recorded outcome). Minimal reproducer pinned in tests/security A-2.

risks.title: RL-075-F1: outbox records stranded in DELIVERING have no public recovery path
risks.justification: A crash between the outbox claim commit and the outcome commit leaves records in DELIVERING; claimDue only considers PENDING records and the RL-003 persistence outbox port exposes no requeue/stuck-sweep API, so a restarted worker cannot continue those obligations through the public interface (the EDGE outbox does expose recoverInFlight; the persistence outbox does not). No data is LOST — the records, payloads and digests remain intact — the invariant broken is 'restart continues in-flight work'. Fixing it means editing packages/persistence — outside the release-gate worker's scope.
risks.exposure: Stranded in-flight outbox obligations after a crash window require manual intervention; durability of the records themselves is intact.
risks.remediation: Add a requeueInFlight(olderThan) sweep on the port (mirroring the edge outbox's recoverInFlight), or claim with a visibility timeout so stranded claims expire back to PENDING. Minimal reproducer pinned in tests/deployment CS-4.

risks.title: RL-073 DEFECT-1: batched inbox drains cannot progress past the first batch of a larger backlog
risks.justification: AdcosWebhookInboxService.processPending(limit) re-slices the ADMITTED list from index 0 on every call; with a backlog larger than limit, the first limit records are re-considered forever and records beyond index limit are never processed. The reliability property 'every admitted record reaches a terminal state in bounded calls' fails at the inbox level; projection-level convergence still occurs via the reconciler's canonical refresh, and the deployment suites pin the workaround (an unbounded drain). Fixing it means editing packages/webhook-inbox — outside the release-gate worker's scope.
risks.exposure: Webhook backlogs greater than the batch limit do not drain through repeated bounded processPending calls; customer-facing read models still recover through reconciliation.
risks.remediation: Track a durable processing cursor (or mark processing state on extended records) so repeated drains advance. Minimal reproducer pinned in tests/load (webhook-ingestion-load) and re-pinned by tests/deployment CS-3.

risks.title: Inherent-infrastructure verification limits (the documented honest gaps of RL-074/RL-075)
risks.justification: The verification docs record the limits that cannot be closed on this tree: audit full-tail rewrite without an external anchor (I-5, limit pinned exactly), timing side channels (error-level oracle closure proven; wall-clock timing not deterministically measurable), denial-of-service volumes (admission policy verified; network-level exhaustion out of scope), secrets at rest in a real backend (port discipline verified; a vault adapter's at-rest properties are deployment work), webhook signing-key compromise operations (verifier/rotation mechanics verified; fleet-wide emergency rotation is operational work), real-database semantics (WAL/fsync nuance out of scope for in-process suites), no SQL migrations yet (runner semantics verified), single-process crash injection (CAS contract-level coverage), whole-state restore granularity (PITR is a storage-engine capability), health-check authenticity per deployment (composition honesty proven). These are the canonical 'requires real infrastructure' class the RL-081 dispatch names: recorded explicitly, never hidden.
risks.exposure: Each limit has its strongest deterministic proxy verified and its boundary pinned by an explicit test; the residual risk materializes only when real infrastructure lands without revisiting these items.
risks.remediation: Revisit each item as the corresponding real infrastructure lands (vault-backed secrets adapter, PostgreSQL persistence driver, anchored audit checkpoints, network-level load testing); the pinned limit tests flip when the stronger implementations arrive.
risks.reviewBy: when real infrastructure replaces the in-memory adapters
